from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.play(FadeIn(data))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)

        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Polynomials behave exactly like vectors.", "Map coefficients as 3D coordinates.", "Geometry and algebra align perfectly."]
        self.setup_layout("Concrete vs. Abstract Examples", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Polynomial: P(x) = ax^2 + bx + c -> (a, b, c)
        def get_poly_vector(a, b, c):
            return axes.c2p(a, b, c)

        # Animation 1: Polynomial vector
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        poly_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=get_poly_vector(1, 0.5, -1), color="#FFCC00")
        self.add(poly_vec)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFCC00")
        self.wait(1)

        # Animation 2: Coefficients as 3D coordinates
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        dot = Dot(color="#CCFF00")
        dot.move_to(get_poly_vector(1, 0.5, -1))
        label = MathTex("(a, b, c)", color="#CCFF00").next_to(dot, RIGHT)
        self.add(dot, label)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#CCFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # Animation 3: Align geometry
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        poly_vec_2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=get_poly_vector(-1, 1, 0.5), color="#00CCFF")
        dot_2 = Dot(color="#00CCFF").move_to(get_poly_vector(-1, 1, 0.5))
        self.add(poly_vec_2, dot_2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00CCFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Signals are sums of vectors.", 
            "Infinite dimensions hide in audio.", 
            "Math powers our modern technology."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application and Conclusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animation Elements
        signal_icon = VGroup(
            *[Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color=BLUE).shift(i*0.2 * RIGHT) for i in range(5)]
        )
        hilbert_circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color=PURPLE)
        concept_map = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#88AAFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(signal_icon, 'C2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(signal_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFAAFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(hilbert_circle, 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(hilbert_circle))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(concept_map, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(concept_map))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: From Concrete to Abstract (1 minute)
sections.content: Transition from familiar 2D/3D vectors (arrows) to the abstract concept. Introduce the core idea: a vector space is not defined by what its elements 'look' like, but by how they 'behave' under addition and scalar multiplication.
sections.example: Visual: An arrow in 2D space transforms into a musical chord or a collection of photos. Even if they don't look like arrows, they follow the same 'algebraic rules'.

sections.title: The 8 Rules of the Game (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Explain the 8 axioms of a vector space (Closure, Associativity, Commutativity, Identity, Inverse, Distributivity). Use a checklist visual to show that if a set satisfies these, it is a valid vector space.
sections.example: Use a character named 'Vector-Bot' who checks if a mathematical object obeys these 8 rules. If one fails, the object is rejected.

sections.title: Concrete vs. Abstract Examples (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Showcase that polynomials and functions function as vectors. Visualize the set of all polynomials of degree ≤ 2 as a space that can be mapped to 3D coordinate geometry.
sections.example: Visual: A set of polynomials (e.g., ax² + bx + c) mapping to a 3D grid, showing that coefficients (a, b, c) act like coordinates (x, y, z).

sections.title: Application and Conclusion (1 minute)
sections.content: Briefly mention how abstract vector spaces are the backbone of modern tech, specifically Fourier transforms in audio processing or Hilbert spaces in Quantum Mechanics.
sections.example: An audio signal from a cat meowing being broken down into a sum of sine waves—each sine wave is a vector in an infinite-dimensional space.
